text.content:
This part takes you from the blank page to the sheet ready to play. The GM prepares creation (chapter 1.1); the player fills in the wizard step by step (1.2 to 1.4); the GM reviews and validates (1.5). Without the Character Designer module, or to touch up a sheet, chapter 1.6 shows how to fill everything in by hand.

The creation wizard comes from a separate module, Shadowrun 5 — Concepteur de personnage, the Character Designer (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.LY0gP2n4uytah6mP.JournalEntryPage.FY83GXbOqmVz6WN9]{its entry}). It keeps the budget for you, but does not copy the rules: creation is read in the book (Core Rulebook p. 60-107), and in Run Faster for Sum to Ten and point buy (Run Faster p. 62-65).

Example followed in the screenshots: Kira, a human adept built with priorities, at Standard level, with the book's tables.

 @UUID[.T5KfTXWqout4skEo]{Implants}

GM

What it is for

Before the player opens the wizard, the GM decides three things for the world (the default method, the tables, the level of play), then puts each new character in creation. This flag gives access to the wizard and makes the shop apply the creation caps.

Step by step: setting up the module

  1. Activate the Shadowrun 5 — Concepteur de personnage module in the world; it needs the Mégapack (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.LY0gP2n4uytah6mP.JournalEntryPage.FY83GXbOqmVz6WN9]{module entry}).

  2. Open the Settings tab of the sidebar, then Configure Settings, and choose Shadowrun 5 — Concepteur de personnage in the left column.

  3. Set the three lines, then click Save Changes:

    • Creation method: the method offered by default for each character (Priorities, Sum to Ten, Karma). Default: priorities.

    • Priority tables: Book tables (default) or House rules.

    • House Rules, rule 7 (Essence of the mundane): ticked by default, it only acts with the House Rules tables.

Step by step: choosing the level of play

The level of play (Street, Standard, Prime) is not a setting of the module: it is the one of the system's shop, which also sets the purchase caps at creation (Core Rulebook p. 64).

  1. Open the Shadowrun settings window (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.UtP5ShuRjXa3JrEZ.JournalEntryPage.q5GXYM16NSmsFUJp]{how to open it}), Shop tab.

  2. Choose Shop: creation level: Street level (Availability 10, rating 4), Experienced runner (Availability 12, rating 6) — the book (default) or Prime runner (Availability 15, rating 6).

  3. The Custom (values below) choice is for the shop only: the Character Designer then takes the Standard level tables.

For a character who must play at a different level from the table, the GM sets their level of play in the Character Designer, for that character alone: this choice takes precedence over the world's.

Step by step: putting a character in creation

  1. Create the actor (type Character) and give the player ownership of it, as usual in Foundry.

  2. Open its sheet, click the three dots of the title bar, then In creation. Only the GM sees this entry.

  3. A question opens: Method and starting Karma. Choose this character's Creation method, then:

    • The book's Karma: 13, 25 or 35 depending on the level (Core Rulebook p. 64), or 800 for point buy (Run Faster p. 64);

    • or type another value in Karma for this creation and click This value.

  4. The Create this character button appears in the sheet's title bar, for you and for its owner.

  • Closing the question without answering writes nothing: it will come back the next time you put this character in creation.

  • The method and the starting Karma can be changed afterwards at step 1 of the wizard (Method list and Starting Karma field, visible to the GM only). Changing the method clears the Karma set by hand: 25 is not worth 800.

  • To end creation without going through validation, choose Creation over in the same menu. Usually, validation takes care of it (@UUID[.KazhvoLZOCm5j4Hi]{validating}).

House Rules — the Character Designer's tables

With Priority tables on House rules, the Character Designer takes three priority tables (Street, Standard, Prime) and their horizontality: more free knowledge and contact points, contacts capped at 8 points instead of 7, and Connection 4 at most at Street level. They apply to priorities and Sum to Ten; point buy always follows the book.

Rule 7 halves, without rounding, the Essence of the implants of a character without Magic or Resonance, whatever the method; the Mégapack's already reduced implants (suffix "(NE)") are not halved a second time. At Prime level, Magic at rank E also offers the Non implanté (astral perception only) type: an adept at Magic 1, Astral Perception set by default, one magical skill at 2, no tradition.

The points the House Rules leave in the dark (starting Karma, "Non implanté", the Standard E line for skills) follow DjamZ's rulings; the summary cites them, and the GM validates.

What the system does on its own

  • For a character in creation, the shop applies the level's caps (Availability, rating), debits each purchase from the creation nuyen and delivers at once, even if your table chose delayed delivery.

  • Removing an implant during creation leaves no Essence lost, and the Essence cost is not "taken at its highest" before creation ends (@UUID[.T5KfTXWqout4skEo]{implants}).

  • A player can neither set nor lift the flag; an actor created or imported by a player never arrives in creation.

  • Starting kit: each player character created in the world receives a Backpack storage (the pack), a Locker storage (the safehouse) and an empty Standard credstick (Run Faster p. 228-229, Core Rulebook p. 440). It only receives what it lacks, also after Import Data; a character pulled from a compendium and those already in the world receive nothing. Setting Starting kit, Looting and spoils tab, ticked by default (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.bqnSE0NCUfCmiCd8.JournalEntryPage.auDjqd2HZaWxiGoy]{see 7.3}).

What the GM does by hand

  • The shop till's Creation mode setting (add without debiting) applies to everyone, not to one character: it puts nobody in creation for the wizard. Use the sheet's menu.

  • Special natures (infected, drakes from Dark Terrors, SURGE changelings…) are chosen in the Special nature section of the Metatype step: the wizard counts their cost in Karma, but their powers and traits remain for the GM to validate. Metavariants, metasapients and shapeshifters are chosen at the Metatype step (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.LY0gP2n4uytah6mP.JournalEntryPage.FY83GXbOqmVz6WN9]{9.5}).

Related settings

  • Module: Creation method (Priorities), Priority tables (Book tables), House Rules, rule 7 (Essence of the mundane) (ticked).

  • Shadowrun settings, Shop tab: Shop: creation level (Experienced runner) (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.arMGpK6RvbR3sLNQ.JournalEntryPage.EVmnGJKbAtj857w9]{settings detail}).

References

  • Levels of play and starting Karma (Core Rulebook p. 64); priority creation (Core Rulebook p. 65); wiki: Shop and fencing.

@UUID[.4tM8aqcqF3Rc1XVm]{1.2 The wizard step by step} →

Player

What it is for

The wizard has you create your character in eleven steps, in the book's order. At the top of the window, a banner counts your budget at every click: you see at once what is left, what overflows, and what is paid in Karma. Everything you choose is kept on the character: you can close and resume later.

Step by step: opening the wizard

  1. Open your character's sheet. The GM must have put it in creation (@UUID[.Yeb3R29dzJgAkkcn]{preparing creation}).

  2. Click Create this character, in the title bar.

The window

  • ① The budget banner. Each item shows what is spent out of what is available, then its state: left, ✓ complete, ✕ over, or +n paid in Karma (contacts beyond the free points, for example). The items are grouped: Priorities (or Free points), Karma, Resources, and Essence. Under the banner, the foldable line To settle at the end of creation lists the current alerts, with their number.

  • ② The eleven steps. Click a step to go straight to it; a green tick marks a complete step.

  • ③ The current step. At the top, a line recalls what the step expects or offers. Each panel has its title and a Reset button, which only clears that panel (gear already bought stays on the sheet). Panels with lists have two boxes: what you chose on the left, the lists on the right; on each line, + adds and the eye (See the sheet) opens the item read-only.

  • ④ The footer. Previous and Next step; at the last step, Save to the sheet.

What the wizard does on its own

  • The draft survives: each choice is stored on the character. Close the window whenever you like; when you reopen it, you find everything again.

  • The sheet follows: each time you leave a step, the wizard writes the chosen attributes, skills, metatype and items (knowledge skills, languages, qualities, spells, powers) onto the sheet. It only touches the items it placed itself.

  • Two people on the same character (the GM and you): each window rereads what the other wrote.

  • Searching in French or English: in the lists (qualities, skills, spells, rituals, complex forms, adept powers), the search finds an entry by its French or English name, and the English name is shown after the French one. A skill can also be found by its group ("Firearms" shows Pistols, Automatics, Longarms).

  • No step blocks you: you can go over a budget or leave a remainder. Everything is settled at the summary (@UUID[.SHDPSLzr37K7CMvm]{step 11}).

  • A mark in the name: as long as creation is not validated, the character's name begins with 🔍 (to review) or ⛔ (not compliant: a budget exceeded or a fault). The mark is set each time you leave a step; the GM's validation removes it, as does the "In creation" flag lifted by hand.

Backlinks: @UUID[.0F7GZR2rUUMY91UA]{MENU}

← @UUID[.Yeb3R29dzJgAkkcn]{1.1 Preparing creation} · @UUID[.GID0iUmzGtjlelLk]{The steps one by one} →

Step 1, Priorities, depends on the method: @UUID[.xAVFngTqIcEtaOk0]{Priorities, Sum to Ten, Karma}. Step 9, gear, has its own chapter: @UUID[.nnAVUfmnLgdl6XgA]{gearing up at creation}.

Step 2: Metatype

  1. Click your metatype. Those your priority does not allow are greyed out, marked Not at this rank; each card recalls the special points it gives and its abilities (vision, dermal armor…).

  2. Under the book's metatypes come Run Faster's metavariants, metasapients and shapeshifters (Run Faster p. 88-105), then the metasapient AI (Data Trails p. 145-148), each with its page.

  3. The Special nature section, at the bottom, is for infected characters, changelings, drakes or monads: the wizard counts the nature's cost in Karma, outside the 25 Karma cap on positive qualities; the GM validates its powers.

Step 3: Attributes

  1. Each attribute starts at your metatype's minimum. Raise it with +, one attribute point per step. Only one attribute can reach its natural maximum: it then carries the MAXIMUM tag.

  2. In Special attribute, raise Edge: each point above the minimum costs one special point.

  3. In Magic or Resonance, choose your type among those your priority offers (magician, adept, mystic adept, aspected magician, technomancer), or Neither Awakened nor Emerged. Set the rating: it starts from what the priority offers, and each point beyond is paid in special points (6 at most). A magician also chooses their Tradition; the mentor spirit is chosen at the Qualities step.

  4. Read What it gives: the inherent limits, initiatives and condition monitors, recomputed at every click (Core Rulebook p. 101, 52). In brackets, the value with the implants and powers already on the sheet.

Nothing is blocked upwards: an attribute can go one point over its maximum, as can Edge, Magic or Resonance. The wizard flags it, and it is the GM's validation that accepts or sends back. The minimum, however, stays blocking.

Step 4: Skills

  1. Groups come first (their skills in a tooltip): a group gives its rating to all its skills and is paid in group points.

  2. Look up a skill in the list, then add it; it arrives at 1. Raise it with +.

  3. If your Magic or Resonance priority offers skills, tick the gift (the parcel icon) on the one you choose: it is free up to the offered rating, points beyond are paid.

  4. Choose a specialization in the line's menu (the book's examples), or ✎ Add another… to type it: it costs one point.

  • Magic and Resonance skills are reserved to those who have the attribute (Core Rulebook p. 89); an adept does not get the magical groups.

  • Rating 6 at most, 7 with the Aptitude quality (Core Rulebook p. 73), which can name a skill from a group. The + button does not stop: going over is flagged at the summary as a fault.

  • Raising a skill of a group taken above the group, or specializing it, is paid in Karma (Core Rulebook p. 88-89): it is allowed, and flagged in amber.

  • The Flight skill appears as soon as the GM has ticked its setting (Body, health and augmentations tab).

House Rules — group skills paid in points

The module setting Specializations and skills of a group payable in points (house rule) (unticked by default, the book) lets these points and this specialization be paid with skill points; each skill taken out of its group is then flagged to the GM at the summary.

Step 5: Knowledge and languages

  1. The first line gives your free points: (Logic + Intuition) × 2.

  2. Click Add a knowledge skill, type its name, choose its type (Academic, Interests, Professional, Street, Tactics) and set the rating.

  3. Click Add a language. The first one is ticked Native: it is free (N). A second native language requires the Bilingual quality.

A knowledge skill's menu offers the book's examples with their type, and recalls the linked attribute (Logic or Intuition) (Core Rulebook p. 147-149); Small Unit Tactics, of the Tactics type, opens combat maneuvers in play (Run & Gun p. 99) (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.a0A5owDWyn9339sO.JournalEntryPage.eWTrOUQuSfM2Rf1a]{see 3.4}). A knowledge skill typed twice is added only once.

Step 6: Qualities and martial arts

The step has two tabs: Qualities and Martial Arts.

  1. Look up a quality by its French or English name, or by its cost ("7 karma"), then click +: it is added on the left, with its Karma. The Sort menu orders the list (positive then negative, positive only, negative only, cost ascending or descending).

  2. An Awakened character takes their mentor spirit from the same list ("Mentor spirit…"): 5 Karma, counted with positive qualities (Core Rulebook p. 76); its menu then appears. A technomancer likewise takes their paragon ("Paragon…") (Kill Code p. 102-104).

  3. Correct the Karma of a quality with levels in its line; a cost that differs from the compendium is flagged to the GM. Remove a quality with the cross.

  • 25 Karma at most of positive qualities, and 25 of negative qualities (Core Rulebook p. 71).

  • An AI's qualities, a changeling's metagenic qualities and a drake's have their own Special qualities panel, outside the general list.

The Martial Arts tab

  1. Choose a style among the 42 of Run & Gun, then its techniques: 7 Karma for the style with its first technique, 5 for each one after, 5 techniques and a single style at creation (Run & Gun p. 128-133).

  2. With the Revised martial arts module and its setting ticked (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.LY0gP2n4uytah6mP.JournalEntryPage.G5lt3ucuBihlzQCc]{see 9.10}), the list offers its 48 styles: the style's special technique is free, outside the 5 techniques and at no cost, and a Weapon and Strike technique is taken "(armed)" or "(unarmed)".

Step 7: Character traits

This step is only used with a House Rules module that provides character traits; without one, it stays empty and you can skip it.

Step 8: Spells and powers

  1. A magician first chooses what they add (Spell, Ritual or Preparation), then clicks their formulae; a technomancer their complex forms; an adept their powers.

  2. Set the level of a power that has one with − and +. The top line counts power points (or the spells offered and those paid in Karma).

  3. Tick Fetish for a spell cast with a fetish (Street Grimoire p. 212): Drain −2, minimum 2; a spell cast both with and without a fetish is learned twice.

Each spell shows its category, type, range, duration and Drain, and the tradition's Drain resistance is recalled. Powers arrive active on the sheet. A choice that does not apply to your type (a spell for an adept) stays in the draft without counting or going onto the sheet. The same step buys bound spirits, the bonding of purchased foci, a technomancer's registered sprites and an AI's programs (Core Rulebook p. 98, 318, Data Trails p. 146).

Step 10: Contacts

  1. Click Add a contact, then type their name and choose their Archetype, their Kind of service, their Metatype, their Hobby or vice and their Personal Life in the menus (each has "Add another…") (Run Faster p. 172-180).

  2. Set their Connection and Loyalty. Each contact costs their sum in Karma; Family adds 1 Karma, Blackmail 2 (Run Faster p. 178).

  3. Optional: choose the character's pronoun and answer the 20 questions (Run Faster p. 19-20). The answers go into the biography, without overwriting what you wrote there.

  • The contacts' free Karma is Charisma × 3, × 6 at Prime level (Core Rulebook p. 64, 98); the surplus is taken from your Karma. The GM can set another Contact Karma multiplier for this character, at the top of the step; you see it without being able to change it, and the summary recalls it.

  • A contact is worth 7 points at most. An Organization (Run Faster p. 176-177) has Loyalty 1 and counts within the 25 Karma of positive qualities, not in the free Karma. The wizard's contacts are contact items on the sheet (Social tab).

References

  • Creation step by step (Core Rulebook p. 60-107); @UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.hqT1pRAqlBA4yN9s.JournalEntryPage.jegaeuBLsiKBOt9y]{the character sheet}.

← @UUID[.4tM8aqcqF3Rc1XVm]{1.2 The wizard step by step} · @UUID[.xAVFngTqIcEtaOk0]{1.3 Priorities, Sum to Ten, Karma} →

All

What it is for

The wizard knows the three creation methods. The GM chooses each character's (@UUID[.Yeb3R29dzJgAkkcn]{preparing creation}); only step 1 and the banner change, the other steps stay the same.

Priorities

The book's method (Core Rulebook p. 65): five columns (Metatype, Attributes, Magic or Resonance, Skills, Resources), five ranks from A to E, each used once.

  1. At step 1, click a cell of the table: its column takes that rank.

  2. The column that had that rank takes your old rank: you swap, you lose nothing. Each column's rank is shown at its head.

Sum to Ten

Run Faster's Sum to Ten (Run Faster p. 62-63), Sum to Ten in the module: A is worth 4 points, B 3, C 2, D 1, E 0.

  1. Click a cell as with priorities. Here a rank can be used several times; each column still has only one rank.

  2. Watch the Priority points (10) item of the banner: the total must be exactly 10. No remainder is allowed; a different total stays flagged.

Point buy (Karma)

No table: everything is paid in Karma (Run Faster p. 64-65), 800 points or the value set by the GM.

  • Step 1 only shows the method and the starting Karma; the banner counts Karma (point buy).

  • The metatype has a cost (step 2); Magic or Resonance is bought like a quality, then each point beyond 1 (step 3); attributes and skills are paid at the advancement table.

  • 235 Karma at most in resources, per the errata, typed in at step 9.

What applies to all three methods

  • Leftover Karma: 7 at most carry over into play, the rest is lost (Core Rulebook p. 98). In point buy too, whereas Run Faster loses all of it (Run Faster p. 65): DjamZ's ruling.

  • Karma cap (priorities and Sum to Ten): Street 26, Standard 50, Prime 70 (Core Rulebook p. 64). The book does not print the Standard one: 50 comes from 25 + 25 of negative qualities (Core Rulebook p. 71), by DjamZ's ruling. No cap in point buy.

  • Born Rich (Run Faster p. 145): 30 more Karma convertible into nuyen, at every level (Street 35, Standard 40, Prime 55; 275 in point buy). DjamZ's ruling: the book only gives the Standard figure.

  • In Debt (Run Faster p. 156): 5,000 ¥ per Karma point, 15 points at most. This Karma becomes nuyen and is not added to the Karma to spend; it counts within the 25 Karma of negative qualities (DjamZ's ruling). The debt is tracked in play.

House Rules — Sum to Ten and Karma

With the House Rules tables, Sum to Ten takes the same tables and the same horizontality as priorities; the rank values from 4 to 0 are read there as the Sum to Ten points, which the House Rules do not explain. Point buy always follows the book, without the tables or the horizontality.

References

  • Priorities (Core Rulebook p. 65); Sum to Ten (Run Faster p. 62-63); point buy (Run Faster p. 64-65); Born Rich (Run Faster p. 145); In Debt (Run Faster p. 156).

← @UUID[.GID0iUmzGtjlelLk]{The steps one by one} · @UUID[.nnAVUfmnLgdl6XgA]{1.4 Gearing up at creation} →

Player

What it is for

Step 9, Gear and lifestyle, gathers the money of creation: your creation nuyen, Karma converted into nuyen, purchases (made in the system's shop), lifestyle and starting nuyen.

Step by step: converting Karma

  1. In Karma into nuyen, raise Karma converted with +: 2,000 ¥ a point, 5, 10 or 25 points at most depending on the level (Core Rulebook p. 64, 94) (more with Born Rich).

  2. The top line (Creation nuyen) immediately gives the total available, spent and left.

Step by step: buying

  1. Click Open the shop. The shop opens with your character as the buyer; under the till, a line recalls Character in creation and its caps (Avail 12, rating 6 at Standard).

  2. Search, add to the cart, then click Pay. Each purchase is debited from the creation nuyen and arrives at once on the sheet (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.bqnSE0NCUfCmiCd8.JournalEntryPage.zKky8MvmSeq77inw]{the shop}).

  3. Go back to the wizard: each item bought has its line there, with its price and Availability; parts installed on board a vehicle too. Clicking its name opens its sheet, or the Workshop of a vehicle or drone.

  4. To return an item, click its bin: a confirmation states the sum, then the item leaves the inventory and its price goes back to the creation nuyen. In a purchase of several items, each returns its share; an item is never refunded twice.

The GM also sees, with a warning, two bins reserved to them: an expense whose item cannot be found (the expense is returned) and a shop item with no expense found (it goes without refund).

An item beyond your level's caps (Core Rulebook p. 418) is refused by the shop; the GM can place it themselves if they accept it, or allow these purchases through the shop's setting (flagged at the summary). The Availability of each line shows its letter (R or F), and the current value of a modified item is shown under the price paid.

Step by step: buying a Run Faster PACK

  1. In Gear PACKs (Run Faster), choose a PACK from the list on the right: the book's 127 PACKs, sorted by its sections, with a search (Run Faster p. 228-253).

  2. On the left, its contents are shown item by item, with the matching Mégapack item (its sheet behind the eye), the price, the Availability and, depending on the PACK, the Essence or the foci's bonding Karma. Choose the variants the book offers (weapon category of an ammo crate, autosofts…).

  3. Click Buy this PACK: it is paid at the book's price, each piece arrives on the sheet and is added to the list of gear bought, where it is removed with its share like a shop purchase.

The items that have no Mégapack counterpart (bags, toolkits, reagents, explosives…) are listed before the purchase and noted on the expense: add them by hand.

Implants and Essence

As soon as an implant is bought, an Implants and Essence block is added to the step: each implant and its Essence cost, which the banner totals. With rule 7 of the House Rules, the cost for a character neither Awakened nor Emerged appears struck through, then halved.

Step by step: the lifestyle

  1. Choose your lifestyle in the list; the monthly rent is recalled.

  2. Set the number of months paid with − and +: one month at least, no cap above it but your budget (Core Rulebook p. 370). For a dwarf or a troll, the rent is multiplied according to the metatype, and the line says so.

  3. To set a lifestyle's points (options, entertainment, Safehouse, Traveler, Commercial…), click Compose: the lifestyle's sheet opens, and the rent it computes is the one the wizard counts (Run Faster p. 216-224).

  4. If the sheet has several lifestyles, mark the main one: it is the one that gives the starting nuyen roll (Core Rulebook p. 95).

Step by step: starting nuyen

  1. Read the Starting nuyen line: up to 5,000 ¥ of creation nuyen are kept, plus a roll depending on the lifestyle (Core Rulebook p. 94-95).

  2. Click Roll the starting nuyen. The roll goes to the chat; its result is shown at the step. The GM can redo it (Roll again (GM)).

  3. Nothing is paid in yet: it is the GM's validation that writes these nuyen onto the sheet (@UUID[.SHDPSLzr37K7CMvm]{next step}).

References

  • Karma into nuyen and 5,000 ¥ kept (Core Rulebook p. 94-95); purchase caps at creation (Core Rulebook p. 418); @UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.bqnSE0NCUfCmiCd8.JournalEntryPage.auDjqd2HZaWxiGoy]{money and lifestyle}.

← @UUID[.xAVFngTqIcEtaOk0]{1.3 Priorities, Sum to Ten, Karma} · @UUID[.SHDPSLzr37K7CMvm]{1.5 Submitting, sending back, validating} →

All

What it is for

The last step, Summary, takes stock of the character. The player submits it to the GM, who sends it back with a word or validates it. Validation writes the Karma and the starting nuyen, then returns the sheet to normal play.

The summary

  • The status, at the top: draft, submitted, sent back (with the GM's word) or validated.

  • The summary sheet: the character as they will play, read from their sheet — attributes (augmented in brackets), limits, initiatives, monitors, skills with their dice pool, qualities, spells in the book's format, powers, weapons, armor, gear, vehicles, contacts, lifestyle.

  • The budget: each item and its state. OK; Over by…; +n, paid in Karma; … left, kept in play (Karma up to 7, nuyen up to 5,000 ¥); … left: does not carry over, in orange, only here: during creation, a remainder is never a fault.

  • To correct: the faults (a budget exceeded, a skill at 7 without Aptitude…). No fault: the character is legal. when there are none.

  • For the GM to validate: what only the GM decides (a special nature, a starting nuyen roll not made yet…).

  • Rules applied and rulings: the Character Designer's choices that depart from the book or complete it, with their page.

  • At validation: the Karma and nuyen that validation will carry into play.

Step by step: submitting to the GM

  1. Fix what is To correct, then click Submit to the gamemaster, at the bottom of the summary.

  2. The draft becomes read-only for you: The gamemaster has it. The GM receives a card in the chat.

Step by step: after being sent back

  1. A notification warns you, and the GM's word arrives in the chat. Reopen the wizard: the word is at the top of the summary.

  2. Fix what it asks, then click Submit to the gamemaster again.

Backlinks: @UUID[.0F7GZR2rUUMY91UA]{MENU}

← @UUID[.nnAVUfmnLgdl6XgA]{1.4 Gearing up at creation} · @UUID[.KazhvoLZOCm5j4Hi]{GM side: reviewing and validating} →

Step by step: reviewing

  1. The submission reaches you as a whispered card in the chat, with a Review button. Click it: the wizard opens at the summary.

  2. Go through the steps if needed. At the bottom of the summary, choose Send back with a word or Validate.

Step by step: sending back with a word

  1. Click Send back with a word, type what needs fixing, then click Send back with a word in the window.

  2. The player receives your word as a card and finds it again at the summary; the draft becomes editable again.

Step by step: validating

  1. Click Validate. A question sums up the faults (budgets exceeded, contacts, others) and what validation is going to write.

  2. Click Yes. If faults remain, validating anyway is your ruling.

Validation writes, in the sheet's transactions, the nuyen beyond 5,000 ¥ taken away (Nuyen not kept at creation), the lifestyle roll (Starting nuyen (lifestyle)) and the Karma kept (Karma carried over from creation). Then it lifts the creation flag: the sheet is in normal play, the shop charges again and has no caps, and the player receives a card. A validated creation can no longer be changed in the wizard.

  • You can validate or send back without waiting for a submission: the buttons are at the summary as soon as you open it.

  • With two GMs connected, only the active GM can validate: they are the one who writes the transactions, so that they are not written twice.

  • Export build.json saves the validated creation to a file: purchases made afterwards in play are not in it.

The sheet ready to play

The sheet now carries everything the wizard wrote on it: attributes, skills, items, contacts, Karma and nuyen. From then on, an implant keeps the highest Essence cost it reaches (@UUID[.T5KfTXWqout4skEo]{implants}), and advancement is played as usual (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.hqT1pRAqlBA4yN9s.JournalEntryPage.jegaeuBLsiKBOt9y]{the sheet}).

All

What it is for

Without the Character Designer module, or to touch up a sheet already in play, everything is filled in by hand on the sheet. The system computes dice pools and Essence; the creation budget is yours to keep (Core Rulebook p. 60-107).

Step by step: filling in the sheet

  1. Open the sheet and switch to edit mode with the padlock in the title bar (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.hqT1pRAqlBA4yN9s.JournalEntryPage.vt6wZWsR9zLHGudq]{filling in the sheet}).

  2. In the Attributes block, type each value in the Nat. column: the Aug. column is computed (augmentations included). Choose Magic or Resonance in the block's list, then type its value; type Edge too.

  3. Choose the metatype in the Biography tab: it sets vision; its attribute bonuses remain to be counted by hand.

  4. In the Skills tab, type each skill's rating and specialization.

  5. Drag qualities, spells, powers, contacts and items from a compendium (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.hqT1pRAqlBA4yN9s.JournalEntryPage.FI0Yyn9xEWcJLmHX]{items}).

  6. Write the starting Karma in the Biography tab, Evolution block: a gain line under Past Runs, and one line per expense under Improvements. The Current Karma is computed.

  7. Write the nuyen in the Gear tab, finances block, as gain and expense lines (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.bqnSE0NCUfCmiCd8.JournalEntryPage.auDjqd2HZaWxiGoy]{money and lifestyle}).

Buying without the wizard

Put the character in creation anyway (@UUID[.Yeb3R29dzJgAkkcn]{sheet menu}): the shop will apply the level's caps and debit its purchases. The GM can also place an item without debiting it (the till's Equip box), or add everything without debit with Creation mode.

Step by step: installing an implant

  1. Buy the implant at the shop, or drag it from a compendium onto the sheet: it goes into the Augmentations tab.

  2. Check its line: Rat. (rating), Ess. Cost (Essence) and Cap. (capacity, with its accessories below).

  3. Read the Remaining Essence in the Derived tab.

What the system does on its own

  • Magic and Resonance: any fraction of Essence lost costs one point (Essence Loss modifier).

  • Essence at zero: the shop refuses a purchase that would drop Essence to 0 or less.

  • Augmentation cap: an augmented attribute rises by +4 at most (Core Rulebook p. 94). The surplus is removed, and the attribute's tooltip shows the real value and the value kept. Magic, Resonance and Edge are not affected.

  • Essence taken at its highest: outside creation, an implant keeps the highest Essence cost it reached; lowering its rating or its grade gives nothing back. The GM can set it back to the current cost from the implant's sheet (Set the Essence back to the current cost).

  • Implant removed: outside creation, the Essence stays lost; an Essence lost (removed implants) line appears in the Augmentations tab, and the GM can give it back (Give this Essence back (GM)). In creation, nothing is lost.

  • These GM-reserved values are kept by a register of the system, in the connected GM's browser: with no GM connected, a removal leaves no Essence lost.

What the GM does by hand

  • Rule 7 of the House Rules is only applied by the Character Designer, on a character in creation. Outside the module, adjust the Essence cost yourself.

Related settings

  • Shadowrun settings, Body, health and augmentations tab: Augmentation cap (default: +4 at most over the natural attribute), and Essence holes (Chrome Flesh p. 74) (Chrome Flesh p. 72) (unticked: lost Essence stays lost; ticked, implants installed afterwards fill the hole first).
